pages.text: Chinnu loved the sky. Every night he lay on the terrace and counted the stars. The count never came out finished.
pages.caption: Chinnu on the terrace

pages.text: One day his mother took a page from an old book and folded a boat. "This is not an ordinary boat," she said with a smile. "Tell it a wish and set it on the water, and it will go anywhere."
pages.caption: The paper boat

pages.text: That night Chinnu went to the pond. He set the boat on the water and whispered, "Take me to the stars."
The boat moved. First on the water, then on the air. Chinnu's eyes went wide. The reflection of the stars in the pond lifted up and became the real sky.
pages.caption: From the pond to the sky

pages.text: The first star he met was small and yellow. "I am not the Pole Star," it said shyly. "Nobody counts me." Chinnu said, "I will count you as number one."
pages.caption: The small yellow star

pages.text: The boat sailed on. A great red star roared, "What is a child doing here?" Chinnu was not afraid. "I came to finish the count," he said.
pages.caption: The red star

pages.text: The red star laughed. "The count never finishes, little one. Every night a new star is born." Hearing that did not make Chinnu sad. It made him glad.
Far away a cluster of stars was turning in a circle. It looked like a festival. Chinnu stood in the middle of the boat and clapped.
pages.caption: A festival of stars

pages.text: Dawn came. The boat drifted gently down. The pond was ordinary water again. In Chinnu's hand was the paper boat, slightly damp.
From that night on Chinnu stopped counting stars. Instead, every night he names one new star. The first name he gave: Small Yellow Star, Number One.
pages.caption: Number one
